sentences.text: JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act through her natural guardian,
seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident dated 06-11- 2022.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that: On 06- 11-2022 at about 5.00 pm., the minor petitioner as pedestrian was proceeding at Kaidale along with grandmother near Kaidale cross, Davanagere Taluk and District, at that time the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 17-HF-6227 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Bapuji Hospital, Davanagere wherein conservative treatment was given with POP.
So far the parents of the petitioner have spent huge amount towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was a student, studying in 1st standard at Mallikaruna Swamy School, Kaidale, Davanagere Taluk and District.

Due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner, she is unable to concentrate on her studies and unable to participate in cultural,
sports and other activities.

3. The respondent no.1/ the RC owner of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-17-HF-6227 has filed written statement and contended that he was proceeding in Kaidale cross by observing all traffic rules and regulations passing on either said of the road, the grandmother of the petitioner left the child on the road carelessly without holding the hands of the child, the child ran towards the road and came in contact with the motor cycle and herself was caused for the accident and that the said motorcycle was insured with the 2 nd respondent and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
4. Respondent No.2 /the Insurer of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-17-HF-6227 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the rider of insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license.
The insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.
The petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gains.

It is further submitted that the grandmother of the petitioner was main architect for the causing for the accident and they negligently tried to cross the road without observing the movement of the vehicle.
Hence respondent no.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the guardian of the minor petitioner proves that on 06-11-2022 at about 5-00 pm., when the petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian along with her grandmother Smt. Rathnamma, near Kaidale cross, Davanagere Taluk, the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-17-HF- 6227 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?

3. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined her natural guardian/father Mr.Mallikarjuna S R as PW.1 and two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.

The respondents have not led any evidence on their behalf.
7.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, P.W.1 the father of minor petitioner has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on the stated date when the minor petitioner as pedestrian was proceeding at Kaidale along with grandmother near Kaidale cross, Davanagere Taluk and District

, at that time the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-17-HF-6227 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained,
treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
10.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Spot Mahazar, sketch,
IMV report, charge sheet, requisitions, treatment letter issued from Hospital Authority, etc.,

sentences.text: On the basis of the complaint lodged by father of the petitioner by name Mallikarjuna, case has been registered against the rider of vehicle in Crime No.185/2022 of Hadadi Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section under section 279, 338 of IPC.
12.

Though the respondent no.2 has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident but the respondent no.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle no where has disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident but taken the contention that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the grandmother of the petitioner.
It is true that the accident in question has occurred on 06.11.2022 at about 5.00 p.m, but complaint came to be lodged on 09.11.2022 and there is delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint.
In the complaint and FIR the reason for delay has been explained stating that the complainant was engaged in providing treatment to the petitioner.

Though the complaint was lodged after 3 days of the accident but if the medical records are perused i.e., OPD Initial assessment of Bapuji Hospital is perused, on the date of the accident itself the petitioner was shifted to Bapuji Hospital and patient's father gave alleged history of accident as "road traffic accident while patient was walking by the side of the road hit by two wheeler at around 4.45 p.m".
Hence in the medical records maintained first in point of time the involvement of two wheeler is mentioned.
Hence involvement of offending vehicle cannot be disputed.
13. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, at the time of accident the petitioner along with her grandmother was proceeding towards Kidale Village.
The offending vehicle which came from opposite direction hit to the petitioner.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused the width of the road at the spot of the accident is nearly 12 feet.
The accident in question has occurred on the extreme left side of Kidale cross- Kidale Village.

When petitioner was proceeding towards Kidale Village and offending vehicle came from opposite direction and hit to the minor, it means the driver of the offending vehicle by driving his vehicle on the extreme right side of his road by encroaching nearly 10 feet has hit against the minor.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle driven the vehicle on the left side of his road this accident would not have occurred.
Though respondent no.1 and 2 have disputed the manner of accident but they have not taken any pain to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.
They have not placed any contra evidence to rebut the evidence given by the PW.1 and police records.
Hence there is every reason to believe that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue no 2 :
The guardian of petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his daughter/minor petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has not produced wound certificate and discharge summary.
Admittedly the petitioner has taken conservative treatment with POP on fracture site.
The Medical records produced by the petitioner discloses that she has taken treatment on OPD basis for 4 to 5 times.

It is true that the petitioner has not produced wound certificate but they have produced Ex.P6 to Ex.P7 to prove that the investigating officer had submitted repeated requisition to the hospital authority to furnish the wound certificate so as to file charge sheet but the concerned medical authority has not issued wound certificate on the ground that since the relatives Nandini S M vs Krishna C K on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97762840/

entities.text: Nandini S M vs Krishna C K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 of the petitioner refused for MLC and admission for which they signed in the OPD card they cannot give wound certificate

. But in the Ex.P7 issued by Medical Director, Bapuji Hospital they have clearly stated that they have given treatment to the petitioner and she has sustained fracture injury and she was diagonized to have fracture both bones (left )leg with suture wound and she was treated for the same with POP above knee and that petitioner was regularly taking follow up treatment on OPD basis.
15. From the aforesaid document it can be said that the petitioner has taken conservative treatment on OPD.
She has sustained fracture injuries which is grievous in nature.
16. Dr. B Vishwanth- Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospita, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and through him recent OP card and x-ray film are got marked as Ex.P12 to Ex.P13.
PW.2 deposed that he examined the petitioner on 08-07-2025 clinically, radiologically for assessment of disability.
PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 26% and whole body disability at 13%.

If the evidence of the PW.2 carefully perused, he is not a treated doctor and he has not inspected the old X-ray of the petitioner and that the fracture injury of the petitioner is united and there is no complication in the fracture site and there is no loss of bone and muscle power and there is no shortening of the limps.
As per the PW.2 the petitioner has disability of 26 % on the left lower limb and 13 % to the whole body.
If 1/3 rd of disability on whole body is considered it comes 8%.

Hence it can be said that petitioner has disability of 8% on whole body but not 13% as assessed by the PW.2.
17.
Hence, this court inclines to consider the disability of petitioner at 8%.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
18. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, she has produced medical bills for Rs.4,068/- as per Ex.P.9.
Hence petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.4,068/-.

19. In a Judgment rendered in Master Mallikarujuna / Divisional Manager National Insurance company, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that "though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of children suffering from disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various high courts, we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc should be if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body Rs 3 lakh , Up to 60% Rs 4 lakh , up to 90% Rs 5 lakh and above 90% it should be Rs 6 lakh .
For permanent disability up to 10% it should be Rs 1 lakh unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
In the said case the disability is to the tune of 18 % and minor was in the hospital for longer period causing inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents.

Hence the minor was compensated under the head pain and suffering already under gone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience and discomfort in life on account of permanent disability to the tune of Rs 1,00,000/-.

sentences.text:
As disability of the petitioner on whole body is assessed as 8%, keeping in mind the observation made in the Mallikarujuna case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering already under gone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship,
inconvenience on account of permanent disability.
21. The guardian of the Petitioner has stated that they have spent considerable amount towards her conveyance and nourishment etc..
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
22. So far as discomfort and inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents during the period of hospitalization of the petitioner is concerned, awarded to the tune of Rs 75,000/-.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.1,00,000/-
already under one and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship inconvenience on account of permanent disability 2.

Medical expenses Rs. 4,068/-
3. Discomfort, inconvenience, and Rs. 75,000/-
 loss of earnings to the parents  during the period of  hospitalization  4 Incidental Expenses Rs. 20,000/-

Total Rs.1,99,068/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,99,068/- (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Nine Thousand Sixty Eight only).
23.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
24. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,99,068/- (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Nine Thousand Sixty Eight only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent no.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that the guardian of minor petitioner incurred medical expenses for the treatment of the petitioner and that they required the award amount for the eduction of the minor, hence submitted to release entire amount in favour of petitioner through guardian.
Hence, considering the grounds urged ordered to release entire amount in favour of natural guardian for the welfare of minor.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that the guardian of minor petitioner incurred medical expenses for the treatment of the petitioner and that they required the award amount for the eduction of the minor, hence submitted to release entire amount in favour of petitioner through guardian.
Hence, considering the grounds urged ordered to release entire amount in favour of natural guardian for the welfare of minor.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
